title: Seven in ten Americans affirm the Trinity. Most also call the Spirit a force.
subtitle: U.S. adults, 2014 to 2025
caption: Agreement that there is one true God in three persons has held at about 70% in all six surveys. In every survey a majority also agreed that the Holy Spirit is a force and not a personal being, a claim the doctrine of the Trinity rules out.
note: Statements: "There is one true God in three persons: God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit" and "The Holy Spirit is a force but is not a personal being" (share who agree). All twelve figures are printed in the 2025 white paper, which compares each year with the earlier surveys.
